subject.title: Allow verified WebP assets in autoreview bundles

question: Should autoreview permit any WebP container to bypass payload review based only on structural checks and `dwebp` decoding, despite opaque metadata and extension chunks remaining unseen?
rationale: This is a review-security policy boundary rather than a mechanical implementation detail: maintainers must choose whether binary asset metadata can be trusted as a substitute for reviewing all embedded content.

options.title: Retain fail-closed binary handling
options.body: Keep the existing rejection for WebP files until an approved inspection model covers every container payload.

options.title: Adopt a bounded asset-review design
options.body: Allow WebP only after a maintained design exposes or strips all non-pixel chunks and defines decoder isolation, resource limits, and validation proof.

options.title: Accept metadata-only review
options.body: Land the exemption while explicitly accepting that embedded WebP metadata and extension chunks are outside autoreview coverage.

recommendation.title: Retain fail-closed binary handling
recommendation.body: Keep the existing rejection for WebP files until an approved inspection model covers every container payload.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent autoreview binary-hardening history makes steipete the strongest available routing candidate for this security-boundary choice.
